svg.title: Endpoint absorption and the complete invariants of type III products
svg.desc: At zero a countable decomposition of the identity into equivalent projections gives an onto unitary from H tensor ell2 to H and the full matrix algebra absorption map. At one geometric probability intervals leave unpaired mass at most a divided by delta. Summable losses and density errors yield a tracial binary tensor factor. Together with the interior absorption theorem these prove r infinity equals S for the stated type III product scope, while rho has neither endpoint.

g.text: The two endpoints complete the invariant formulas
M is type III and a countable separably represented type-I product.
Endpoint 0: R₀ = B(ℓ²)
1 = Σₙ pₙ, with every pₙ equivalent to 1
sₙ*sₙ = 1, sₙsₙ* = pₙ
U(ξ ⊗ eₙ) = sₙξ is an onto unitary.
x ⊗ eᵢⱼ ↦ sᵢxsⱼ*
Finite compressions give the full normal map.
Endpoint 1: R₁ is the tracial binary product
Choose a block with largest probability a < εδ.
Pair within (a(1−δ)ʲ⁺¹, a(1−δ)ʲ].
At most one unpaired word per interval.
Unpaired mass ≤ Σⱼ a(1−δ)ʲ = a/δ < ε
Paired probability ratios lie in (1−δ, 1].
Summable losses turn these pairs into a tracial tensor factor
Σ εₙ = 1/4 gives φ(f) ≥ 3/4; Σ hₙ ≤ ½ Σ δₙ² < ∞ gives the onto GNS map.
M ≅ fMf ≅ R₁ ⊗ B ⇒ M ⊗ R₁ ≅ M
The corner comparison uses type III; odd/even interleaving absorbs the extra binary factor.
r∞(M) = S(M), including 0 and 1
ρ(M) = { exp(−2π/t) : t > 0 and t belongs to T(M) } ⊂ (0,1)
T(M) = {0} ∪ { ±2π / |log x| : x belongs to ρ(M) }
The target in ρ is Rₓ; the target in r∞ is M. Neither endpoint belongs to ρ(M).
Proof: TP Sections 13–15. Geometric intervals are a probability partition, not a sampled spectrum.
The type III scope is essential: r∞(R₀) = {0}, whereas S(R₀) = {1}.
